author: DAVID BRIGGS
title: Briggs: Transfer portal chaos wiped out the roster. Eddie George is confident BGSU got better - NewsBreak
text:
By DAVID BRIGGS ,
9 hours ago
BOWLING GREEN — As Eddie George turned the page to his second season, forgive the Bowling Green football head coach if he looked around and felt cast in a sequel nobody ordered: Dude, Where’s My Team?
Gone was all but one starter, his son, Eriq, a defensive end. Everyone else had graduated or declared for free agency. More than 35 Falcons followed the crowd — 6,700 Division I players strong — into the transfer portal.
It was a sign of the times, amplified by the timing. Remember, BGSU hired George in March, after the main transfer window closed.
“The nature of the beast,” he said.
Do not, however, mistake his disappointment for discouragement.
When I checked in with George the other day, he sounded energized, like a coach who sees chaos and thinks opportunity.
The reality: The doors at Sebo Athletic Center don’t just lead out. For all Bowling Green lost, it gained a lot, too, including 15 transfers to go with the top-rated high school recruiting class in the Mid-American Conference.
Not surprisingly, George especially went heavy on passers.
After a four-win debut season undercut by quarterback injuries — when even a pair and a spare was not enough — he stocked up like a blizzard was rolling in.
BG added two transfers — Oregon’s Austin Novosad, a former top 200 recruit, and Assumption’s Jay Kastanin, the MVP of his Division II conference last year — and one of the top prep prospects in Ohio. Jalin Mock, a 6-3 dual threat from Pickerington North, is the nation’s No. 60 quarterback in the 2026 class, per 247Sports.
The trio will join Hunter Najm, the fourth-string sophomore who finished last season as the emergency starter.
“We've addressed every issue that we've had this offseason, hopefully with better players,” George said. “[Now], we’ve got to develop them into who we need them to be, and that's my job. But we took a step in the right direction by continuing to get the right people in the building.”
No, that’s not to suggest the Falcons had the wrong people last year.
Look at some of their top players and where they landed: defensive end David Afogho (West Virginia), linebackers Gideon Lampron (Colorado) and Caden Marshall (Southern Methodist), cornerbacks MJ Cannon (Cincinnati) and Keyon Washington (Iowa State), offensive tackle Nate Pabst (Florida State), running back Cameron Pettaway (Iowa State), and tight end Jacob Harris (Wisconsin).
That’s a lot of talent, and George would have loved to keep most of it.
“There were some guys we were counting on coming back, where we felt like we put together a decent financial package for them,” he said. “But the offers they're getting from Power Four schools and the opportunity to compete at the highest level, it's tough to compete against that.”
By the way, don’t get George started on the transfer … whoops, too late.
He’s ready for college sports to leave unrestricted free agency behind and adopt a union model, with real contracts and collective bargaining.
“Let’s put a structure around it that mimics what we see at the professional level,” George said. “That's the perfect model. Let’s stop dancing around what this is, because it's hurting high school players, and the system is not set up for success for the current players.
“It's teaching them that, ‘Hey, when it gets hard, jump in the portal and go seek money.’ And you can't throw money at everything. Sometimes, you've got to dig your feet in the dirt where you're at and gut it out and find a way to handle the adversity. That's where the gold is. That's where the true wealth is.”
But, anyway, where were we?
Right, next year’s roster.
Point is, George finally has the chance to truly cast the program in his image.
If we’re going to fairly appraise his work, start now.
A year ago, George was hired in March, a week before the start of spring football, and hit the ground at sonic speed. It wasn’t a transition. It was a fire drill.
That’s a hard ask, and one plenty of schools would sidestep. (While I contend BG made the right call in appointing a permanent coach, I understand the alternative. See: Northern Illinois. Faced with a similar situation Wednesday after head coach Thomas Hammock left for an assistant job with the Seattle Seahawks, NIU immediately made defensive coordinator Rob Harley the interim boss this season, rather than hire from outside this late in the game.)
“I always felt I was one step behind last year,” George said.
No more.
With a year now to continue getting “the right people on the bus” — including on his staff — he has had time to reflect and refine, not to mention define the identity of the program.
And that is?
Well, if you watched George run back in the day, you probably already know: power first, always.
“I talk about building the spine of our team,” George said. “You need a strong, physical running back, of course. You have to have a quarterback who can add value in the run game — a plus-one quarterback — and is tough and makes great decisions. Center, guard, guard, you have to have physicality, you've got to be able to move and change the line of scrimmage.
“On the flip side, you need two monsters at defensive tackle to plug the A gaps, a thumping ‘Mike’ linebacker, and a safety who can come downhill and disrupt and disturb the peace. … You build inside out.”
As for the state of the build, we’ll see.
With just two starters returning — safety Kal-El Pascal is back, too, withdrawing from the portal — I’d be lying if I tried to predict how this all comes together.. (I like a lot of the transfers, including Novosad and Purdue linebacker Sanders Ellis, who previously starred for George at Tennessee State, but who knows?)
George will confide only that he likes this team.
“We’ve still got to get out on the grass and see how it plays out,” he said, “but we certainly did address things the best way we could.”
Where others might see total chaos, George is just settling in.
